Note: This is written by Cassie as she was moderating her JSC 249\.

# Admin

*I benefitted from the templates and advice other mods shared here, so I wanted to share my own for new mods. Feel free to make a copy and adapt it for your JSC.*

***Getting Started:** I used https://www.when2meet.com/ for scheduling first meeting and standing meetings, then sent Google Calendar invites with relevant docs attached. We meet for 90 mins on my Zoom Pro account. I have music playing as folks arrive, and I include a personal check-in prompt in addition to a series of professional update prompts (Rose/Thorn/Bud). I never end on logistics and instead wrap up with a Plus/Delta poll on https://www.mentimeter.com/ and check-out prompt.*

* *If you meet \>60 mins, ask if anyone in your JSC with a Zoom Pro account is willing to host the meetings.*  
* *Other options: [https://meet.jit.si/](https://meet.jit.si/) , two 45-min back-to-back calendar invites using Google Hangout (you can build in a 5-min break in-between the meetings)*

***Comms:** I used email to send a reminder with prep work 1-2 days before our meeting, and I attached the agenda to our recurring Google Calendar invite. I used our private Slack channel for all other comms and for polling, and we’d share job updates, requests for help, or planned absences.*

***Attendance:** When people were absent due to interviews, we didn’t reschedule if it’d be too last-minute, and instead kept the meeting time as is and adapted agenda to the group’s needs with whoever showed.*

* *If only 2 people can attend a meeting, it’s worth rescheduling. Meetings with ≥3 people were more enriching (more perspectives, feedback, etc.).*  
* *If any meeting will land on a holiday, reschedule it well in advance or cancel it.*  
* *Once someone gets a job, it’s unlikely they’ll be able to attend future meetings, especially if your meetings are during business hours, even if they initially committed to 10 meetings.*  
* *If someone misses a meeting without notifying you or following up, check in with them directly. Per the Moderator Guide, if they miss 2+ meetings, you likely need to consider removing them (regardless of if they say they want to be involved), and email Emily Teter at [emily@collaborativegain.com](mailto:emily@collaborativegain.com) with an update.*

# Mnookin Meeting Facilitation

See Meetings 2-3 for agendas. Here’s an overview of how I facilitated. 

Mnookin Exercises \-

* I created a [master doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Pgkl6dcpqgFp8lqQ50nPER6gGJVjU948sIOPL-clShU/edit?usp=sharing) where everyone could take their notes during the paired interviews. Rationale: Keeps things organized (single source of truth), and can inspire group by looking at others’ lists.  
* As a group of 5, I had a breakout of 2 and of 3, and I rotated them the 2nd round, so that they could get to know other members.  
* I then requested that everyone upload their 2-pager draft to our Google Drive at least 1 hour before Meeting 3\. I specified speaking order by whomever uploaded their docs first.

Mnookin Presentations \-

* As a group of 5, we had 3 present during Meeting 3 and 2 during Meeting 4\. People spent about 6-7 min presenting and 11-13 mins giving feedback (so 17-20 min total per person). I recommend allotting 20 min per person, and if you have time remaining, you can revisit the 2-pagers that were shared at the start as people may have more Qs or requests for help after listening to others.  
* I offered a feedback framework (inspired by Stanford d.school)—“[I like, I wish, I wonder](https://medium.com/@sugar_network/i-like-i-wish-i-wonder-c44e78b76627)”—which the group was welcome to use. After each presentation, I asked the member if they had specific requests/Qs or areas they wanted advice/feedback on before we did a go-round of general feedback. I also asked the member after the discussion whether they were open to us leaving feedback via Google Doc comments later.  
* I’ll be building in time in future meetings to revisit the Mnookin 2-pagers at the request of my JSC.

You can also facilitate it such that people do the Must-Haves/Must-Notes exercise on their own and bring a draft of their Mnookin to the meeting for the whole group to give feedback on, or you can have people pair up and meet up on their own time to do the exercises.

# What if people want to jump ahead?

The anxiety of not applying to roles because the NSA process encourages you to pause and slow down is a common experience. Ultimately, you can’t stop people from networking and interviewing, but unless they’re intentional about what they’re looking for (after doing the Mnookin) and what the market is hiring for (through the Listening Tour), they may end up in rebound roles that aren’t actually aligned with their values/interests/skills. They’re welcome to read ahead in the book, and you can make space for their Requests for Help that may be further along but I wouldn’t let it dominate otherwise that could affect the group morale/cohesion if people are ultimately doing their own thing.

I think it’s fine to accelerate the Mnookin and Gratitude House meetings; you could have them do the must-haves/must-nots on their own time, and then use Meeting 2-3 to get feedback on it from the whole group (I’d allot at least 20 min/person for them to present and have a discussion/Q\&A on their Mnookin).

I’d actually suggest that you have them do their Gratitude House exercise now on their own, so they can start the Listening Tour outreach now even before their Mnookin is done because it may take a week or more for them to schedule those. My JSC initially started with two 90-min meetings per week and then once we started Listening Tour, we went back to 1x/week because that Tour takes longer than people realize due to all the scheduling and waiting for responses and we wouldn’t have enough to report back on with only a few days between meetings.  
[The Mod Guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OU_5_W5yj477rMF7o8ynbVAJ8e5jXmqnO_6MXTxiEwY/edit#heading=h.mtl0sgsq06p1) also addresses this Q.

## Meeting 2: 2023-04-24

## Mnookin Two-Pager

**Pre-Work:**

* Read Ch 4 of [Never Search Alone](https://www.amazon.com/Never-Search-Alone-Seekers-Playbook-ebook/dp/B0B75PK2XJ/) and reflect on what you hate doing & what you don't want in your job to prep for “must-nots/must-haves” in-meeting exercise  
* Download the [Mnookin Two Pager Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1c5e4Cz0GZfuRIo5NqgHIY6A8H2HPWN9WyljSTEdMRa4/edit) (more examples at the JSC Slack [\#000-mnookin-two-pager](https://jsc-official.slack.com/archives/C04DQM1H7CH))  
* Start thinking about the first three people you want to speak to during your Listening Tour  
* Review our Charter and add feedback as comments, if any

**Reminder:**

* Join the LinkedIn LIve hosted by Phyl Terry – every \*other\* Friday at 12pm ET (check [Phyl.org](http://phyl.org) homepage for the link to register)

**Attendance:** All present

### Agenda

x:00 \- ⚡️Check-Ins (15 min \- 3 min each)

* What was a highlight from your weekend?  
* Emotional Pulse: On a scale of 1-10, how is your emotional balance\* this week, and why did you give that rating?  
* Updates: Do you have any professional updates since we last met?  
* RFH: Do you need any help with any aspect of your search?  
  *\* From NSA: “Every one of us has an emotional balance sheet made up of assets (hope, confidence, motivation, etc.) and liabilities (envy, fear, insecurity, dejection, etc.).”*

x:15 \- [Exercise: What You Hate (and Love) Doing](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Pgkl6dcpqgFp8lqQ50nPER6gGJVjU948sIOPL-clShU/edit#) (20 min)

* **Interview** (15 min total): If 3 people, 5 min each; if 2 people, 7 min each; partner takes notes and keeps time.  
  * What are the kinds of jobs, industries, and functions that you *hate* doing?  
  * What about past jobs did you *dislike*?  
* Repeat interviews and rotate note-takers until everyone has gone.  
* **Invert** (5 min) your lists separately to what you *love* doing. 

x:35 \- [Exercise: Must-Nots & Must-Haves](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Pgkl6dcpqgFp8lqQ50nPER6gGJVjU948sIOPL-clShU/edit#heading=h.ai1t828hxfiv) (35 min)

* **Interview** (15 min total): If 3 people, 5 min each; if 2 people, 7 min each; partner takes notes and keeps time.  
  * What do you *not* want in your next job?  
  * Have you ever had a bad job or a bad boss? If yes, what did that teach you about what you do *not* want in a culture, boss, etc?  
* Repeat interviews and rotate note-takers until everyone has gone.  
* **Invert** (5 min) *your partner’s* Must-Nots into Must-Haves.  
* **Refine** (5 min) your Must-Haves separately.  
* **Present** (10 min, 3-5 min each) your Must-Haves for discussion and feedback.   
  * What might be missing? What should be edited?

x:10 \- 🎁 Requests for Help (RFH) (10 min)

* Address any RFHs that came up during Updates or elevate RFHs

x:20 \- 📚 Homework & Logistics (5 min)
